## Tailnet

`tailnets.tsunaro.io` · scope **Cluster** · short name `tn` · `v1alpha1`

Tailnet is a cluster-scoped binding to one control server.

### Spec

TailnetSpec describes a control server and how the operator authenticates to it.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiKeyLifetime` | string | no | Lifetime of the self-minted working API key. Rotated at half-life. Default `720h`. Max length 32. |
| `apiSecretRef` | object | yes | Bootstrap API key, read only. The operator mints its own rotating working key from it and never writes back here — so this may live in GitOps without a rotation fight. |
| `apiSecretRef.key` | string | no | Default `apiKey`. |
| `apiSecretRef.name` | string | yes |  |
| `apiUrl` | string | no | In-cluster URL for the REST API if it differs from Server. Empty → Server. |
| `authKeyLifetime` | string | no | Lifetime of the reusable ephemeral pre-auth keys handed to agents. Rotated at half-life. Default `168h`. |
| `bridgeNameAllowlist[]` | []string | no | DNS zones a TailnetIngress.spec.exposes[].bridgeNames entry must lie within (proper subdomain), e.g. ["site.example.internal"]. Bridge names are extra certificate SANs and SNI routes for clients that reach the ingress through a bridge and resolve the name in their own zone; the operator neither renders nor claims them. Ingress CRs are written by tenants, so this is the admin's veto over which foreign zones may be served. Empty → no bridge names (TLSReady=False/BridgeNameDenied). Items ≤ 16. |
| `defaults` | object | no | Defaults inherited by ingress resources that do not select their own TLS source. |
| `defaults.tls` | object | no | TLSDefaults supplies an issuer for HTTP ingresses without an explicit TLS source. Secrets are namespace-local and cannot be selected as a Tailnet-wide default. |
| `defaults.tls.issuerRef` | object | no | TLSIssuerReference identifies a cert-manager issuer without requiring its API dependency. Issuer references resolve in the ingress namespace; ClusterIssuer references are cluster-scoped. |
| `defaults.tls.issuerRef.group` | string | no | Only cert-manager.io issuers are supported. Default `cert-manager.io`. One of `cert-manager.io`. |
| `defaults.tls.issuerRef.kind` | string | no | Default `Issuer`. One of `Issuer`, `ClusterIssuer`. |
| `defaults.tls.issuerRef.name` | string | yes | Name of the issuer. Max length 253. |
| `dns` | object | no | DNS records rendered from egress aliases and ingress names. Off when empty. |
| `dns.hostsConfigMap` | string | no | Name of the ConfigMap (operator namespace, key "hosts") that receives the rendered hosts file. Empty → the feature is off and a previously rendered ConfigMap is removed. |
| `dns.ingressAliasTemplate` | string | no | Optional template for a shorter DNS alias of an HTTP expose that opts in with `alias: true`. Same placeholders as ingressNameTemplate; {name} is the expose's effective label (dnsLabel or the CR name). The operator requires the alias to end in the SAME literal zone as ingressNameTemplate, because only that zone is guaranteed to resolve over the tailnet. Empty → aliases are disabled. The alias becomes an additional certificate SAN and SNI route; a name claimed by two CRs is resolved oldest-first and the loser reports DNSNameConflict. Max length 253. |
| `dns.ingressNameTemplate` | string | no | Template for a TailnetIngress's DNS name; {name} is the CR name, {namespace} its namespace. Keep the result one label below your gateway's wildcard certificate, e.g. "{name}-{namespace}.prod-1.tailnet.example.internal". Empty → ingresses get no name. Max length 253. |
| `exposeSourceAllowlist[]` | []string | no | Client prefixes a TailnetEgress.spec.expose.allowFrom entry must lie within. Egress CRs are written by tenants, so this is the admin's veto over which site hosts may use a bridge. Empty → no egress may be exposed (Exposed=False/Denied). Items ≤ 64. |
| `headscale` | object | no | External Headscale metadata; compatibility is checked against the API, not the version hint. |
| `headscale.ref` | string | no | Reserved for an operator-managed Headscale. Must remain empty until managed mode is supported. |
| `headscale.version` | string | no | Optional version hint for diagnostics, e.g. "0.29.3". Does not bypass capability checks. |
| `hostnameTemplate` | string | no | Template for a TailnetEgress's tailnet hostname when it sets none. {name} is the CR name. Default `egress-{name}`. |
| `ingressHostnameTemplate` | string | no | Template for a TailnetIngress's tailnet (MagicDNS) hostname when it sets none. {name} is the CR name. Default `ingress-{name}`. |
| `ingressTagTemplate` | string | no | Template for a TailnetIngress's tag when it sets none. {name} is the CR name. The tag IS the authorization — its grants (dst = this tag) decide which peers may reach it. Default `tag:ingress-{name}`. |
| `policy` | object | no | Policy generation from CRs. Off when baseConfigMap is empty. |
| `policy.baseConfigMap` | string | no | ConfigMap (operator namespace, key "policy") holding the base policy in HuJSON. Empty → the feature is off and nothing is rendered or written. |
| `policy.fragmentConfigMaps[]` | []string | no | ConfigMaps (operator namespace, key "policy") holding fragments exported by spoke Tailnets (mode Export on another cluster, committed here after review). Each is merged after the base and this cluster's own CRs; base and own entries win. A listed fragment that is missing or malformed fails the render closed (no write) rather than dropping the spoke's grants. Only valid alongside baseConfigMap. Items ≤ 32. |
| `policy.ingressSourceAllowlist[]` | []string | no | Glob patterns a TailnetIngress.spec.allowFrom entry must match, e.g. ["group:*"]. Ingress CRs live in tenant namespaces, so this is the admin's veto over who tenants may grant access to. Empty → no ingress grants are generated (only the tag is declared). |
| `policy.mode` | string | no | DryRun renders into renderedConfigMap only; Apply also writes the control server when the live policy differs; Export renders only this Tailnet's generated entries (no base, no write) into renderedConfigMap so a hub operator can merge them via fragmentConfigMaps; PolicyApplied reports HubMerged/HubPending by comparing the fragment with the live policy. Start with DryRun, compare, then switch. Default `DryRun`. One of `DryRun`, `Apply`, `Export`. |
| `policy.renderedConfigMap` | string | no | ConfigMap (operator namespace, key "policy") that receives the rendered policy (Apply/DryRun) or the exported fragment (Export) for review. Empty → "<baseConfigMap>-rendered" (Apply/DryRun) or "<tailnet>-policy-fragment" (Export). |
| `policy.routeApprovers[]` | []string | no | Approvers for the generated autoApprovers.routes entries (one /32 per egress target), i.e. the tag your subnet routers carry, e.g. ["tag:fabric"]. Required when on. |
| `policy.spokes[]` | []object | no | Spoke clusters whose exported fragment this hub pulls itself (instead of a committed fragmentConfigMaps entry): the hub reads the spoke's fragment ConfigMap with the kubeconfig in kubeconfigSecretRef, validates it against this hub's limits and the spoke's tagPatterns / routeAllowlist, and merges it per the spoke's approval mode. Only valid alongside baseConfigMap; never in mode Export. Items ≤ 32. |
| `policy.spokes[].approval` | string | no | Auto merges every valid fetched fragment at once. Manual merges the last approved fragment only and reports a changed fetch as pending until an admin annotates the Tailnet with "tsunaro.io/approve-spoke.<name>: <pendingHash>". Default `Auto`. One of `Auto`, `Manual`. |
| `policy.spokes[].configMap` | string | no | Fragment ConfigMap on the spoke (key "policy"). Empty → "<name>-policy-fragment". Max length 253. |
| `policy.spokes[].kubeconfigSecretRef` | object | yes | Secret (operator namespace) holding a kubeconfig for the spoke's API server. Mint it for a ServiceAccount that may only get/list/watch the fragment ConfigMap (the chart's policy.fragmentReader on the spoke renders exactly that). |
| `policy.spokes[].kubeconfigSecretRef.key` | string | no | Default `kubeconfig`. |
| `policy.spokes[].kubeconfigSecretRef.name` | string | yes | Max length 253. |
| `policy.spokes[].name` | string | yes | Spoke name; used in status, events, metrics and the approve annotation "tsunaro.io/approve-spoke.<name>". Max length 63. |
| `policy.spokes[].namespace` | string | no | Namespace on the spoke holding the fragment ConfigMap. Empty → this operator's namespace. Max length 63. |
| `policy.spokes[].routeAllowlist[]` | []string | no | Prefixes (besides this hub's TailnetSites) a spoke route or grant destination that is not a host address may lie within. Host routes (/32, /128) are always accepted unless reserved. Items ≤ 64. |
| `policy.spokes[].tagPatterns[]` | []string | no | Glob patterns the spoke's own tags must match, e.g. ["tag:*-prod-2-*"]; tags already owned by the hub's base document are exempt. Empty → ["tag:*-<name>-*"]. Items ≤ 16. |
| `policy.tagOwners[]` | []string | no | Owners of the generated tags (tagOwners value), e.g. ["group:operator"]. Required when on. |
| `proxy` | object | no | ProxySpec are the defaults for the per-CR agent pods this Tailnet spawns. A TailnetEgress may override image and resources. |
| `proxy.image` | string | no | Container image carrying the tailnet-agent binary. Empty → the operator's own image, so a single pushed image serves both control and data plane. |
| `proxy.imagePullSecrets[]` | []string | no | Names of existing image-pull Secrets in each agent pod's namespace. Omitted inherits the operator defaults; an explicit empty list disables those defaults. Duplicate names are collapsed when building pods because Kubernetes merges these references by name. |
| `proxy.mtu` | integer | no | tsnet outer path MTU. 1200 leaves headroom for a ~1320-byte outer path (typical cloud CNI overlay). Default `1200`. Range 576–1500. Format `int32`. |
| `proxy.probeInterval` | string | no | How often the agent probes each target for reachability. "0s" disables probing. Default `5m`. |
| `proxy.resources` | object | no | ResourceRequirements describes the compute resource requirements. |
| `proxy.resources.claims[]` | []object | no | Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This field depends on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate. This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers. |
| `proxy.resources.claims[].name` | string | yes | Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available inside a container. |
| `proxy.resources.claims[].request` | string | no | Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim. If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise only the result of this request. |
| `proxy.resources.limits` | object | no | Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `proxy.resources.requests` | object | no | Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `reservedNetworks[]` | []object | no | Address space that must never become a tailnet route (node prefix, every cluster's pod and service ranges on this control server); never a network a router advertises. Blocks overlapping TailnetSite prefixes and routes in spoke fragments. Items ≤ 64. |
| `reservedNetworks[].name` | string | yes | Max length 63. |
| `reservedNetworks[].prefixes[]` | []string | yes | Items 1–32. |
| `server` | string | yes | Login/control URL, becomes the agent's ControlURL (e.g. https://ts.example.com). |
| `tagTemplate` | string | no | Template for a TailnetEgress's tag when it sets none. {name} is the CR name. The tag IS the authorization — its grants decide which routes the node sees. Default `tag:egress-{name}`. |

## TailnetAccessRequest

`tailnetaccessrequests.tsunaro.io` · scope **Cluster** · short name `tnar` · `v1alpha1`

TailnetAccessRequest is a request for a TailnetGrant or its extension, kept by the console; its approvals are in the console's audit log. The operator ignores it.

### Spec

TailnetAccessRequestSpec is what a person asked for. The console writes it once; it never changes. The operator does not read this kind: only an approved request becomes a TailnetGrant.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string | yes | Create asks for a new TailnetGrant; Extend asks for a new expiresAt of grantName. One of `Create`, `Extend`. |
| `description` | string | no | Max length 253. |
| `duration` | string | yes | AccessDuration is a lifetime the console offers, counted from the last approval. One of `1h`, `8h`, `24h`, `7d`, `30d`, `permanent`. |
| `grantName` | string | no | The console grant to extend. Max length 253. |
| `ports[]` | []integer | no | Items 1–16. |
| `requestedAs` | string | yes | The requester's console role at the time of the request; it decides how many approvals the request needs. One of `User`, `Admin`. |
| `requester` | string | yes | Provider identifier (`<issuer>/<subject>`, as Headscale builds it) of the person who asked. Max length 512. |
| `sources[]` | []string | no | Recipients of the grant to create, as in TailnetGrant.spec.sources. Items 1–16. |
| `tailnetRef` | object | yes | TailnetRef selects a cluster-scoped Tailnet by name. |
| `tailnetRef.name` | string | yes |  |
| `target` | object | no | GrantTarget is what a TailnetGrant gives access to: one ingress node by tag, or hosts and networks inside a TailnetSite by prefix. |
| `target.prefixes[]` | []string | no | Prefixes inside an unblocked TailnetSite of the same Tailnet. A /32 or /128 is a single host. One prefix outside every site blocks the whole grant (TargetOutsideSites). Items 1–16. |
| `target.tag` | string | no | Tag of a TailnetIngress bound to the same Tailnet (TailnetIngress.status.tag), or an ingress tag a merged spoke fragment grants to. An unknown tag is never rendered (TargetUnknown). Max length 63. |

### Status

TailnetAccessRequestStatus is the decision, written by the console only. It names nobody: who approved, rejected or withdrew is in the console's audit log.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decidedAt` | string | no | Format `date-time`. |
| `grantName` | string | no | The TailnetGrant created or extended on approval. Max length 253. |
| `phase` | string | no | Empty while nobody decided: the request is pending. One of `Pending`, `Approved`, `Rejected`, `Withdrawn`. |

## TailnetEgress

`tailnetegresses.tsunaro.io` · scope **Namespaced** · short name `tneg` · `v1alpha1`

TailnetEgress is a per-identity egress into a Tailnet. It lives in the operator's namespace; a NetworkPolicy decides which namespaces may use it.

### Spec

TailnetEgressSpec is the desired egress into a tailnet for one identity.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `consumerNamespaces[]` | []string | yes | Namespaces whose pods may reach this proxy's Services (NetworkPolicy ingress). Items ≥ 1. |
| `expose` | object | no | Publish the target Services on the site LAN for clients without a tailnet node. Off when empty: the Services stay ClusterIP, reachable from consumerNamespaces only. |
| `expose.allowFrom[]` | []string | yes | Client prefixes allowed to dial the exposed Services (NetworkPolicy ipBlock). Required and bounded: no default route, IPv4 at least /16, IPv6 at least /48. Items 1–32. |
| `expose.loadBalancer` | object | no | EgressExposeLoadBalancer passes implementation-specific LoadBalancer settings through to the Service. The operator interprets none of them; address assignment is the cluster's LB implementation. |
| `expose.loadBalancer.annotations` | object | no | Annotations copied onto the Service (address pools, pool selectors, BGP options …). |
| `expose.loadBalancer.class` | string | no | spec.loadBalancerClass of the Service. Empty → the cluster default implementation. Max length 253. |
| `expose.loadBalancer.labels` | object | no | Labels copied onto the Service, e.g. for LB-IPAM pool selectors. The operator's own app.kubernetes.io/* labels cannot be overridden. |
| `hostname` | string | no | Explicit tailnet hostname. Empty → rendered from the Tailnet's hostnameTemplate. |
| `image` | string | no | Override the Tailnet's default agent image. |
| `resources` | object | no | Override the Tailnet's default agent resources. |
| `resources.claims[]` | []object | no | Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This field depends on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate. This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers. |
| `resources.claims[].name` | string | yes | Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available inside a container. |
| `resources.claims[].request` | string | no | Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim. If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise only the result of this request. |
| `resources.limits` | object | no | Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `resources.requests` | object | no | Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `tag` | string | no | Explicit tailnet tag. Empty → rendered from the Tailnet's tagTemplate. The tag is the authorization: its grants in the tailnet policy decide which routes this node receives. |
| `tailnetRef` | object | yes | TailnetRef selects a cluster-scoped Tailnet by name. |
| `tailnetRef.name` | string | yes |  |
| `targets[]` | []object | yes | Items 1–50. |
| `targets[].address` | string | yes | IPv4/IPv6 address or lowercase MagicDNS name, not a CIDR, URL or host:port. Max length 253. |
| `targets[].aliases[]` | []string | no | Extra DNS names that resolve to this target's Service ClusterIP, rendered into the Tailnet's dns.hostsConfigMap. Use them when the far end routes by name (TLS SNI, HTTP Host): a consumer dialling the alias sends the real hostname, and the L4 tunnel passes it through untouched. |
| `targets[].name` | string | yes | DNS-1035 label; used verbatim as the Service name, so consumers dial <name>.<ns>:<port>. Start with a letter for compatibility with Kubernetes 1.31 Service admission. Max length 63. |
| `targets[].port` | integer | yes | Range 1–65535. Format `int32`. |

| `targets[].present` | boolean | yes | True once that route is present in the pod's netmap (always true for a DNS-named target). |
| `targets[].reachable` | boolean | yes | True once the agent last dialled the target successfully. |

## TailnetGateway

`tailnetgateways.tsunaro.io` · scope **Cluster** · short name `tngw` · `v1alpha1`

TailnetGateway describes a persistent kernel router in the operator namespace. Suspended by default; suspend=false explicitly opts into the fresh writer.

### Spec

TailnetGatewaySpec is an experimental API contract, suspended by default. Explicit suspend=false opts into the fresh writer; existing routers are never adopted. Deletion retains everything unless deletionPolicy=Delete explicitly consents to tearing down the operator's own fresh resources.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `authKeySecretRef.key` | string | no | Default `TS_AUTHKEY`. Max length 253. |
| `authKeySecretRef.name` | string | yes | GatewayName is a namespace-local Kubernetes object name. Max length 253. |
| `deletionPolicy` | string | no | Retain leaves every resource, node and key in place when the CR is deleted. Delete records consent through a finalizer: the operator removes only the fresh resources it created (matched by recorded UID or its own gateway-uid label), the Headscale node and the minted bootstrap key, in a fixed order and fail-closed. User-supplied objects are never deleted. Default `Retain`. One of `Retain`, `Delete`. |
| `dns` | object | yes | GatewayDNS leaves the cluster CoreDNS Corefile and Headscale split-DNS config externally managed. Dynamic hosts remain owned by the existing DNS reconciler. |
| `dns.aliasZones[]` | []string | no | Zones answered only from the Tailnet hosts source, without an upstream: typically another cluster's tailnet zone whose names this cluster reaches through TailnetEgress aliases. Unknown names in such a zone get SERVFAIL. Reconciled live, not identity. Items ≤ 16. |

| `dns.extraZones[].upstreams[]` | []string | yes | Items 1–8. |
| `dns.extraZones[].zone` | string | yes | GatewayName is a namespace-local Kubernetes object name. Max length 253. |
| `dns.image` | string | yes | GatewayImage requires a version tag or immutable digest; the runtime never rewrites it. Kernel Tailscale, CoreDNS and socat use separate images, not the agent image. Max length 512. |
| `dns.serviceClusterIP` | string | yes | GatewayIP is an unzoned unicast IP literal, not a hostname or a prefix. Max length 45. |
| `dns.serviceName` | string | yes | Explicit name of the gateway's DNS Service; pinned identity. Max length 63. |
| `dns.staticRecords[]` | []object | no | Items ≤ 128. |
| `dns.staticRecords[].address` | string | no | GatewayIP is an unzoned unicast IP literal, not a hostname or a prefix. Max length 45. |
| `dns.staticRecords[].name` | string | yes | Relative single label below dns.zone. Max length 63. |
| `dns.staticRecords[].target` | string | no | Target FQDN of a CNAME. Must be equal to dns.zone or end with ".<dns.zone>" and must differ from this record's own FQDN. | `dns.zone` | string | yes | GatewayName is a namespace-local Kubernetes object name. Max length 253. |

| `forwards[]` | []object | no | Items ≤ 16. |
| `forwards[].name` | string | yes | Max length 50. |
| `forwards[].port` | integer | yes | DNS, health, readiness and metrics ports are reserved by the sidecar. Range 1–65535. Format `int32`. |

## TailnetGrant

`tailnetgrants.tsunaro.io` · scope **Cluster** · short name `tngr` · `v1alpha1`

TailnetGrant is a cluster-scoped, optionally time-bound TCP grant for people or policy groups to a TailnetIngress or to hosts inside a TailnetSite.

### Spec

TailnetGrantSpec gives people or policy groups TCP access to one target, permanently or until expiresAt. The operator that owns the Tailnet's policy renders it as a grant and removes it at expiry without any further event. A grant is administrative: it bypasses a TailnetIngress's allowFrom and a spoke's ingressSourceAllowlist. Every field may be changed; to extend a grant, set a new expiresAt.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | string | no | Max length 253. |
| `expiresAt` | string | no | End of the grant by the operator's clock; from this instant on it is no longer rendered. Omitted → permanent. A time in the past is allowed: the grant is expired at once. Format `date-time`. |
| `ports[]` | []integer | yes | TCP ports on the target. There is no "all ports": a grant never widens when the target later listens on more. Items 1–16. |
| `sources[]` | []string | yes | Who gets access: `group:<name>` (a group the base policy declares) or a Headscale user reference with exactly one `@` — the provider identifier (`<issuer>/<subject>@`, stable), a user name (`alice@`) or an e-mail address. Tags and autogroups are not accepted. An undeclared group is dropped (SourceGroupUnknown); an unknown user grants nothing and is not reported, because Headscale accepts it. Items 1–16. |
| `tailnetRef` | object | yes | TailnetRef selects a cluster-scoped Tailnet by name. |
| `tailnetRef.name` | string | yes |  |
| `target` | object | yes | GrantTarget is what a TailnetGrant gives access to: one ingress node by tag, or hosts and networks inside a TailnetSite by prefix. |
| `target.prefixes[]` | []string | no | Prefixes inside an unblocked TailnetSite of the same Tailnet. A /32 or /128 is a single host. One prefix outside every site blocks the whole grant (TargetOutsideSites). Items 1–16. |
| `target.tag` | string | no | Tag of a TailnetIngress bound to the same Tailnet (TailnetIngress.status.tag), or an ingress tag a merged spoke fragment grants to. An unknown tag is never rendered (TargetUnknown). Max length 63. |

### Status

TailnetGrantStatus reports whether the grant is in the live policy.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conditions[]` | []object | no | Conditions: Ready. True/Granted when the grant is rendered and the live policy equals the render; otherwise False with NotPolicyWriter, Expired, ExpiryPending, TargetUnknown, TargetOutsideSites, SourceGroupUnknown or PolicyPending. |
| `conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. Format `date-time`. |
| `conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. Max length 32768. |
| `conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer | no | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. Range ≥ 0. Format `int64`. |
| `conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. Max length 1024. |
| `conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. Max length 316. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | no | Format `int64`. |

## TailnetIngress

`tailnetingresses.tsunaro.io` · scope **Namespaced** · short name `tning` · `v1alpha1`

TailnetIngress exposes in-cluster L4 services on the tailnet as one tsnet node with a MagicDNS name. It lives in the tenant namespace; the tag's grants decide which tailnet peers may reach it.

### Spec

TailnetIngressSpec exposes in-cluster services through one tsnet node. L4 forwards TCP; HTTP mode terminates TLS and proxies HTTP or explicitly verified HTTPS to the selected backend.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `allowFrom[]` | []string | yes | Peers allowed to reach this node (policy grant src), e.g. ["group:team-a"]. Only used when the Tailnet generates policy; every entry must match Tailnet.spec.policy.ingressSourceAllowlist, otherwise the CR gets PolicyDenied and no grant is written. Items ≥ 1. |
| `exposes[]` | []object | yes | Items 1–50. |
| `exposes[].alias` | boolean | no | Request a shorter DNS alias for this HTTP expose, rendered from the Tailnet's ingressAliasTemplate with the effective label (dnsLabel or the CR name). Requires ingressAliasTemplate to be set; otherwise the CR reports InvalidDNSName. |
| `exposes[].backend` | object | yes | Backend is the in-cluster Service an Expose forwards to. Namespace defaults to the CR's namespace; an explicit namespace can reference a shared gateway or another backend. |
| `exposes[].backend.namespace` | string | no | Namespace of the Service. Empty → the CR's namespace. Set it to funnel HTTPS through a shared gateway (e.g. Envoy in envoy-gateway-system) so TLS terminates there while the tailnet identity stays per app. Max length 63. |
| `exposes[].backend.port` | integer | yes | Range 1–65535. Format `int32`. |
| `exposes[].backend.service` | string | yes | Service name; in the CR's own namespace unless Namespace is set. Max length 63. |
| `exposes[].backend.tls` | object | no | Verified HTTPS to the backend. Omission preserves plaintext HTTP. |
| `exposes[].backend.tls.caConfigMapRef` | object | yes | Public CA bundle in the ingress CR namespace, even if the backend is elsewhere. |
| `exposes[].backend.tls.caConfigMapRef.key` | string | yes | Max length 253. |
| `exposes[].backend.tls.caConfigMapRef.name` | string | yes | Max length 253. |
| `exposes[].backend.tls.serverName` | string | yes | DNS name verified against the backend certificate; does not change the dial address or HTTP Host. Max length 253. |
| `exposes[].bridgeNames[]` | []string | no | Additional names outside the tailnet zone this HTTP expose answers to: extra certificate SANs and SNI routes for clients that reach the node through a bridge and resolve the name in their own zone (the site's DNS points it at the bridge address). Each must be a proper subdomain of a zone in Tailnet.spec.bridgeNameAllowlist and must not lie in the tailnet name or alias zone; otherwise the CR reports BridgeNameDenied. Never rendered into the hosts file or claimed across CRs. Items ≤ 4. |
| `exposes[].dnsLabel` | string | no | HTTP DNS label substituted for {name} in the Tailnet's ingressNameTemplate. Omitted or empty uses the ingress-level name; does not change the expose identifier. Max length 63. |
| `exposes[].mode` | string | no | Listener mode. Omitted means L4 forwarding; HTTP requests TLS termination. Default `l4`. One of `l4`, `http`. Max length 4. |
| `exposes[].name` | string | yes | DNS label; identifies the expose in status and in the agent config. Max length 63. |
| `exposes[].port` | integer | yes | Port the tailnet node listens on — what a tailnet peer dials on this node's MagicDNS name/IP. Range 1–65535. Format `int32`. |
| `exposes[].timeouts` | object | no | HTTP-only timeout overrides. |
| `exposes[].timeouts.backendRequest` | string | no | Wait for backend response headers after sending the request body. Defaults to 30s. Max length 32. |
| `exposes[].timeouts.request` | string | no | Whole-response deadline. Omitted means no deadline. Max length 32. |
| `hostname` | string | no | Explicit tailnet (MagicDNS) hostname. Empty → rendered from the Tailnet's ingressHostnameTemplate. |
| `image` | string | no | Override the Tailnet's default agent image. |
| `resources` | object | no | Override the Tailnet's default agent resources. |
| `resources.claims[]` | []object | no | Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container. This field depends on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate. This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers. |
| `resources.claims[].name` | string | yes | Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available inside a container. |
| `resources.claims[].request` | string | no | Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim. If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise only the result of this request. |
| `resources.limits` | object | no | Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `resources.requests` | object | no | Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `tag` | string | no | Explicit tailnet tag. Empty → rendered from the Tailnet's ingressTagTemplate. The tag is the authorization: policy grants with dst = this tag decide which peers may reach the node. |
| `tailnetRef` | object | yes | TailnetRef selects a cluster-scoped Tailnet by name. |
| `tailnetRef.name` | string | yes |  |
| `tls` | object | no | TLS source shared by the HTTP exposes. An omitted or empty source may use Tailnet defaults. |
| `tls.issuerRef` | object | no | TLSIssuerReference identifies a cert-manager issuer without requiring its API dependency. Issuer references resolve in the ingress namespace; ClusterIssuer references are cluster-scoped. |
| `tls.issuerRef.group` | string | no | Only cert-manager.io issuers are supported. Default `cert-manager.io`. One of `cert-manager.io`. |
| `tls.issuerRef.kind` | string | no | Default `Issuer`. One of `Issuer`, `ClusterIssuer`. |
| `tls.issuerRef.name` | string | yes | Name of the issuer. Max length 253. |
| `tls.secretName` | string | no | Existing TLS Secret in the ingress namespace. Max length 253. |

### Status

TailnetIngressStatus is the observed state.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authKeyExpiresAt` | string | no | Expiry of the reusable pre-auth key currently in the agent's Secret. Format `date-time`. |
| `conditions[]` | []object | no | Conditions: TagKnown, Registered, BackendsReachable, TLSReady, Ready. |
| `conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. Format `date-time`. |
| `conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. Max length 32768. |
| `conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer | no | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. Range ≥ 0. Format `int64`. |
| `conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. Max length 1024. |
| `conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. Max length 316. |
| `dnsName` | string | no | DNS name rendered from the Tailnet's dns.ingressNameTemplate; resolves to TailnetIPs via the hosts ConfigMap. Empty when no template is set. |
| `exposes[]` | []object | no |  |
| `exposes[].backend` | string | yes | The in-cluster backend the agent dials, as service:port. |
| `exposes[].bridgeNames[]` | []string | no | Bridge names served by this HTTP expose (certificate SANs and SNI routes outside the tailnet zone); empty unless requested and allowed. |
| `exposes[].dnsAliases[]` | []string | no | Additional resolved DNS aliases for an HTTP expose; empty unless alias is requested and won. |
| `exposes[].dnsName` | string | no | Resolved DNS name for an HTTP expose; empty for L4. |
| `exposes[].listenPort` | integer | yes | Port the tailnet node listens on for this expose. Format `int32`. |
| `exposes[].name` | string | yes |  |
| `exposes[].reachable` | boolean | yes | Backend reachability. With backend TLS this requires a fresh verified handshake bound to the current configuration, CA bundle and unexpired certificate. |
| `exposes[].reason` | string | no | Bounded backend or frontend failure reason; empty when ready. |
| `exposes[].tlsReady` | boolean | no | Local TLS component readiness for an HTTP expose; omitted for L4. This does not establish remote tailnet reachability or client CA trust. |
| `hostname` | string | no |  |
| `hosts[]` | []string | no | Names the agent actually serves: the HTTP exposes' DNS names and their aliases, sorted. For a CR without HTTP exposes it is the node's DNS name. Unlike dnsName (the node identity and first certificate name), every entry here answers. |
| `nodeId` | string | no |  |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | no | Format `int64`. |
| `tag` | string | no | Effective tag (spec.tag or the Tailnet template) — what the policy and the node carry. |
| `tailnetIps[]` | []string | no |  |

## TailnetSite

`tailnetsites.tsunaro.io` · scope **Cluster** · short name `tns` · `v1alpha1`

TailnetSite is a cluster-scoped remote network advertised by tagged subnet routers.

### Spec

TailnetSiteSpec declares a remote network (a branch, a management net, a single host as /32) that a tagged router advertises into the tailnet. The operator renders autoApprovers for the prefixes, replays approvals on the advertising nodes and reports whether the routes are advertised and approved. Who may *reach* the prefixes is a grant in the base policy or a TailnetGrant.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `advertisedBy` | object | no | SiteAdvertiser names the subnet routers that carry a site's prefixes by tag. A router is any Headscale node with one of these tags — an operator-managed TailnetGateway as well as any tagged router in another cluster. Empty → Tailnet.spec.policy.routeApprovers. |
| `advertisedBy.tags[]` | []string | no | Items ≤ 16. |
| `description` | string | no | Max length 253. |
| `owner` | string | yes | Team or person accountable for the network; named in conflict messages. Max length 63. |
| `prefixes[]` | []string | yes | Prefixes of the site. A /32 is a single host. Overlap with Tailnet.spec.reservedNetworks or with an older TailnetSite blocks this CR (RouteConflict); nothing is rendered for it. Items 1–64. |
| `tailnetRef` | object | yes | TailnetRef selects a cluster-scoped Tailnet by name. |
| `tailnetRef.name` | string | yes |  |

### Status

TailnetSiteStatus records what the control server reports for the site's prefixes.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conditions[]` | []object | no | Conditions: RouteConflict, UnmanagedOverlap, Advertised, Approved, Ready. |
| `conditions[].lastTransitionTime` | string | yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. Format `date-time`. |
| `conditions[].message` | string | yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. Max length 32768. |
| `conditions[].observedGeneration` | integer | no | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. Range ≥ 0. Format `int64`. |
| `conditions[].reason` | string | yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. Max length 1024. |
| `conditions[].status` | string | yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. One of `True`, `False`, `Unknown`. |
| `conditions[].type` | string | yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. Max length 316. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | no | Format `int64`. |
| `routesAdvertised[]` | []string | no | Prefixes of this site some advertiser node currently offers. |
| `routesApproved[]` | []string | no | Prefixes of this site approved on some advertiser node. |
